answer: In an agent economy, weight each identity's influence by how its attestations connect to old, independently funded peers. An attacker's sybils mostly vouch for one another, forming a dense inward cluster, a karst of hollow tunnels beneath a thin crust. On the trust heatmap those self-dealing rings glow violet, and that insularity is the signal detectors down-weight. To beat it he cannot mint accounts freely; he must buy real attestations from unrelated, aged nodes, each costing time and staked collateral, so the fake graph's cost scales with every identity instead of sitting near zero.
